final_claim: Every bounded complete Lorenz-84 trajectory obeys an exact exponentially weighted past-eddy-energy law, every compactly supported invariant measure obeys \(\mathbb E[R\mid X]=a(F-X)\), and for \(F<1\) the stated explicit small-forcing inequality forces the global attractor to be a single equilibrium.

correctness.rationale: The scalar filter U=F-X satisfies Udot=R-aU exactly, yielding the backward memory formula on bounded complete trajectories. Generator identities give the conditional invariant-measure law and its moment consequences. For F<1, the complex eddy equation gives a uniform bounded-complete eddy estimate; comparing two complete trajectories yields a contraction factor 2*sqrt(1+b^2)*G^2/[a(1-F)^3]. Exact energy dissipation supplies a compact global attractor, so a contraction factor below one forces that attractor to be one equilibrium. Symbolic checks return zero residual for the algebraic identities.

originality.rationale: Checked Lorenz-84 literature covers boundedness and physical interpretation, dissipation/energy transfer, local stability and Hopf bifurcation, multistability, homoclinics, non-autonomous attractors, invariant-measure comparisons, attractor geometry, and recent global stability in generalized unforced settings. No inspected statement gives the conditional eddy-energy law E[R|X]=a(F-X), its covariance/variance hierarchy, the past-memory support barrier, the explicit F<1 recurrent slab, or the stated nonzero-forcing global-attractor collapse criterion. Several inaccessible or partially accessible sources are recorded as residual risks.

value.rationale: The conditional law supplies an exact invariant-measure diagnostic tied to the physical eddy-energy variable, while the memory formula constrains every compact recurrent state geometrically. The contraction extension turns these identities into an explicit global nonzero-forcing region excluding multistability, periodicity, quasiperiodicity and chaos, complementing predominantly local or numerical Lorenz-84 analyses.
